newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold market subdued on lower Indian demand.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold market subdued on lower Indian demand.

text.p: Dubai gold traders on Sunday pinned hopes on the Indian wedding season and an improved harvest to rejuvinate a subdued market by the end of the year.
"Demand is not so good because the market in India is slow and most of our sales here depend on the market there," said one Dubai souk (market) trader. "But we hope it will pick up on
more demand, including the wedding season, as the year ends."
Other dealers complained of an "average" market.

The second Indian marriage season, from mid-November to the end of February, usually sees a strong upturn in bullion and jewellery purchases, much of which is supplied from Dubai where prices are lower than in Bombay.

Dealers in Bombay said this week gold demand was seen slowing down due to higher supply until December, when the wedding season soars ahead of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan likely to start in mid-January.

In line with lower international gold prices, Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT bar) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 5,134 dirhams (1,399), down from 5,204 dirhams the previous week.
On the international market, an ounce of gold was last quoted on Saturday at $371.25 from the previous week's $376.35.
"This is the best time to buy gold... this is the first time prices are that low in two years," said another Dubai gold dealer.

Bullion imports into Dubai during this year's first marriage season climbed from 27.4 tonnes in March to 32.6 tonnes in April and 33.3 tonnes in May, the highest monthly import figures so far this year.
It is wedding demand, after Diwali (the Hindu festival of lights) that makes India the world's largest gold consumer.
Dubai is a major re-exporter of gold.

The World Gold Council said on Sunday Gold imports into Dubai in October increased by 13.74 per cent to 28.41 tonnes from 24.98 tonnes in October 1995, mainly because of demand ahead of the Diwali festival.
